title: Employer Direct Contract Terms Across Workers' Compensation Referral Programs
content:
# Employer direct contract terms

Three figures describe how a program of the Workers' Compensation Referral relates to an employer's direct-pay contract: how often a direct-pay employer is invoiced, how many visits the employer's direct-pay program covers before the injury must be reported as a claim, and whether treatment is limited to first-aid measures so the case stays outside OSHA recordability.

| Program | Employer invoice cycle (calendar days) | Direct-pay visit cap | First-aid-only treatment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Employer Direct Early Intervention | 30 | 4 | Yes |
| Workers' Comp Outpatient Therapy | 0 | 0 | No |
| Workers' Comp Post-Surgical Therapy | 0 | 0 | No |
| Work Conditioning Program | 0 | 0 | No |
| Work Hardening Program | 0 | 0 | No |
| Functional Capacity Evaluation | 0 | 0 | No |

## Definitions

- **Employer invoice cycle** — the calendar days between invoices to a direct-pay employer; 0 where the carrier is billed bill by bill.
- **Direct-pay visit cap** — the visits an employer direct-pay program covers before the injury must be reported as a claim; 0 where not applicable.
- **First-aid-only treatment** — whether treatment is limited to first-aid measures so the case stays outside OSHA recordability.

## Reading the table

Only Employer Direct Early Intervention carries these terms: the employer is invoiced every 30 calendar days, the program covers 4 visits, and treatment is first-aid only. The five carrier-billed programs show 0, 0 and No.
